text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- South Africa demands an apology from Nigeria for racist remarks made by information minister Walter Ofonagoro about President Nelson Mandela.
- Drugs worth more than five billion naira have been distributed by the Petroleum Trust Fund to health centres and hospitals across Nigeria.
- Governments of the northern states of Bauchi and Gombe need four billion naira to complete work on a mango and tomato processing plant.

- Capacity utilisation at Nigeria's principal ports, Tin Can Island and Apapa, has fallen to 32 percent last week from around 60 percent at the end of last year. Official sources at the ports blame a rash of policy measures which have encouraged ships to use ports in neighbouring countries.
- Government will from Monday begin to pay debts to local contractors worth around three billion naira.
- Apprehension grips staff of Savannah Bank before a meeting of the board of directors on Wednesday which is expected to order redundancies.
- Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) fails to secure insurance cover for its $160 million tank farm at Escravos because of its poor state of maintenance.
